description: Blue Team Village focuses on defensive cybersecurity operations, incident response, network monitoring, and security tooling. Talks cover purple team adversary simulation, endpoint detection engineering, forensic tool demos for the OpenSOC CTF, and real-world breach investigations.

talks.title: Kibana: OpenSOC CTF Tool Demo
talks.teaser: Demonstrates using Kibana to query, visualize, and analyze security event logs during the OpenSOC defense CTF.
talks.summary:
OpenSOC Incident Response CTF

OpenSOC is a defense capture-the-flag competition designed to train and evaluate practical incident response skills within a realistic enterprise environment.

Centralized Log Analysis with Kibana

Kibana serves as the primary visualization and exploration interface for the Elastic Stack, enabling defenders to search through massive volumes of network and endpoint telemetry during an active breach.

Hands-On Investigation Workflows

The session covers constructing Lucene queries, building situational dashboards, and correlating disparate log sources to reconstruct attacker activities during the competition.

talks.title: Purple On My Mind
talks.teaser: Presents open-source tooling and methodologies to measure defensive coverage and test detection engineering pipelines.
talks.summary:
Adversary Simulation Methodologies

Automated adversary simulation allows security teams to rigorously test and measure their defensive postures across production environments without introducing unnecessary risk.

Evaluating Event Pipelines and Detection Rules

Testing must extend beyond individual alerting rules to evaluate the entire pipeline, from initial endpoint telemetry ingestion to log parsing and alert dispatch.

Open-Source Tooling for Continuous Validation

The authors demonstrate custom open-source tools developed to execute controlled attack techniques at minimal cost, ensuring measurable improvements in response procedures.

talks.title: Quark-Engine
talks.teaser: Introduces Quark-Engine, an open-source Python malware scoring and analysis framework for Android applications.
talks.summary:
Android Malware Scoring Architecture

Quark-Engine is an open-source malware scoring and analysis framework written in Python, designed to dissect Android application packages systematically.

Mapping Behaviors to Legal Perspectives

The engine structures its behavioral evaluation around legal classifications inspired by criminal law concepts, mapping permission combinations and API calls to definitive malicious intents.

Automated Triage and Rule Generation

Analysts can integrate Quark-Engine into automated triage workflows to score samples rapidly, detect stealthy evasion tactics, and generate consistent detection signatures.

talks.title: O365 Squatting
talks.teaser: Presents a Python tool to proactively identify typosquatted domains pre-configured against Office 365 infrastructure.
talks.summary:
Preemptive Domain Squatting Discovery

0365 Squatting is a Python-based utility created to uncover malicious typosquatted domains targeting organizations before active attacks or phishing campaigns begin.

Querying Office 365 Infrastructure

The tool generates permutation lists of typosquatted domains and queries Office 365 services directly, identifying domains configured in Microsoft infrastructure that may not yet resolve in public DNS.

Defensive Mitigation and Bug Hunting

Identifying configured domains early enables defenders to block malicious mail routes, preempt credential harvesting, and detect potential domain takeover conditions.

talks.title: Building BLUESPAWN
talks.teaser: Introduces BLUESPAWN, an open-source active defense and EDR software platform for Windows environments.
talks.summary:
Open-Source Active Defense Architecture

BLUESPAWN was developed as an open-source active defense and endpoint detection and response (EDR) software suite specifically tailored for Windows operating systems.

Integrating Community Standards and Detection Engines

The platform incorporates popular industry frameworks and libraries, including MITRE ATT&CK mappings, DoD STIG security benchmarks, YARA pattern matching, and PE-Sieve memory inspection.

Empowering Analysts Against Systemic Threats

By providing defenders with open, inspectable endpoint telemetry, BLUESPAWN enables analysts to rapidly detect, isolate, and remediate hostile tradecraft across enterprise endpoints.

talks.title: Blue Team Village Intro
talks.teaser: Introduces the DEF CON Safe Mode Blue Team Village track sessions, OpenSOC CTF, and community workshops.
talks.summary:
In this opening orientation for DEF CON Safe Mode, organizers of the Blue Team Village welcome the community and introduce the virtual village schedule, workshops, and contests. Opening at 00:20, the hosts discuss adapting hands-on defensive security labs and electronic badge culture to an online conference environment.

At 04:00, the organizers preview community competitions and swag giveaways, outlining rules for participating in defensive CTF challenges and social media recognition contests.

Concluding at 06:03 and 08:01, the hosts spotlight creative custom hardware badges and wearable electronics built by village members, inviting attendees to connect on Discord and collaborate on defensive labs throughout the weekend. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Reversing With Dynamic Data Resolver
talks.teaser: Demonstrates Dynamic Data Resolver, an IDA Pro plugin leveraging DynamoRIO to unpack and analyze obfuscated malware.
talks.summary:
Binary Instrumentation with Dynamic Data Resolver

Dynamic Data Resolver (DDR) is a plugin for IDA Pro that leverages the DynamoRIO dynamic binary instrumentation framework to monitor and analyze running binaries.

Overcoming Complex Malware Obfuscation

Modern malware often employs multi-layered packing, encrypted payloads, and dynamic API resolving to frustrate static analysis, requiring dynamic visibility into memory execution.

Automating Unpacking and Analysis in IDA Pro

The presentation demonstrates practical workflows for instrumenting hostile binaries, extracting decrypted strings and payloads from memory, and feeding resolved symbols directly back into the IDA workspace.

talks.title: OuterHaven: UEFI Memory Space
talks.teaser: Explores methods for exploiting, monitoring, and enumerating the UEFI memory space to detect pre-boot firmware persistence.
talks.summary:
Pre-Boot Exploitation and Firmware Threats

The Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) provides critical system boot services, making its memory space an attractive target for adversaries seeking covert, pre-boot persistence.

Access Hurdles and Memory Enumeration

Navigating and inspecting UEFI memory involves complex hardware and privilege boundaries, creating significant visibility gaps for conventional operating system security agents.

Scripted Inspection and Monitoring Tools

The talk introduces Windows-hosted scripts and Python utilities designed to enumerate UEFI memory regions, monitor unauthorized modifications, and detect stealthy firmware implants.

talks.title: Indicators of Emulation
talks.teaser: Proposes extracting indicators of emulation from cyber threat intelligence to model adversary behaviors more accurately.
talks.summary:
Evolving Beyond Indicators of Compromise

Traditional cyber threat intelligence (CTI) programs focus heavily on compiling static indicators of compromise (IOCs) such as hashes and IP addresses for triage and alerting.

Defining Indicators of Emulation

Indicators of emulation (IOEs) capture behavioral patterns, environmental dependencies, and actionable procedural nuances extracted from threat telemetry, providing actionable blueprints for red and purple teams.

Operationalizing Intelligence for Threat Simulation

The speaker details methods for extracting IOEs from Windows-based malware analysis reports, translating threat intelligence directly into realistic adversary emulation campaigns.

talks.title: How to Stop a Virus With a Spreadsheet
talks.teaser: Recounts how diligent spreadsheet tracking and structured asset management neutralized the NotPetya global outbreak.
talks.summary:
Surviving the Global NotPetya Outbreak

On June 27, 2017, the NotPetya wiper paralyzed enterprise networks worldwide, exploiting SMB vulnerabilities and lateral movement credentials to destroy systems at machine speed.

Defending Enterprise Assets in Microsoft Excel

Delivered entirely from within a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet, this presentation describes how meticulous tracking, rapid triage grids, and coordinated patch status tracking shielded an enterprise from destruction.

Practical Lessons for High-Velocity Incident Response

Structured asset accounting and pragmatic record-keeping prove indispensable during major security crises when automated management consoles and domain services fall offline.

talks.title: Promo Slideshow
talks.teaser: Displays promotional announcements, village schedules, and community contest details for Blue Team Village Safe Mode.
talks.summary:
Blue Team Village presents an informational slideshow and community orientation reel for attendees participating in DEF CON Safe Mode.

The presentation showcases the virtual village lineup, highlighting defensive security workshops, Project Sauron attack-and-defense training ranges, live threat hunting simulations, and community mentorship initiatives. It provides essential navigation details, Discord server channels, schedule coordinates, and acknowledgments of the community volunteers and sponsors supporting defensive security operations throughout the conference.

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Meet-a-Mentor Program
talks.teaser: Introduces the Blue Team Village Meet-a-Mentor initiative connecting cybersecurity veterans with aspiring defenders.
talks.summary:
Blue Team Village Mentorship Initiative

The Meet-a-Mentor program pairs experienced cybersecurity practitioners with newcomers and transitioning professionals to foster career development and technical growth.

Structuring Mutual Mentorship Engagements

The initiative aligns participants based on shared interests, backgrounds, and specific professional goals, helping mentees overcome workplace hurdles while broadening mentors' coaching abilities.

Building a Diverse and Supportive Defender Community

The panel discusses program mechanics, practical guidelines for successful mentor relationships, and how community-driven mentorship expands opportunities across defensive security disciplines.

talks.title: Incident Response Panel
talks.teaser: Frontline incident response leaders discuss breach triage, common operational mistakes made by victims, and readiness best practices.
talks.summary:
Realities from the Breach Frontlines

A panel of seasoned incident responders shares candid observations and critical lessons learned managing high-stakes corporate breaches and ransomware incidents.

Common Pitfalls in Incident Triage

Victims frequently exacerbate compromises by rebooting critical servers, altering log evidence, or communicating over compromised channels before containment is achieved.

Strategic Incident Preparedness

The discussion outlines proactive steps organizations must implement today, emphasizing immutable logging architectures, tested tabletop simulations, and established out-of-band communication plans.

talks.title: Graylog: OpenSOC CTF Tool Demo
talks.teaser: Demonstrates deploying and querying Graylog centralized log management for real-time threat investigation in OpenSOC.
talks.summary:
Centralized Logging for Incident Response

Graylog provides high-performance log collection, parsing, and search capabilities, enabling defenders to monitor diverse event streams across enterprise environments.

Tool Demonstration for the OpenSOC CTF

This walkthrough shows participants how to navigate Graylog's web interface, construct pipeline rules, and filter complex server logs to uncover attacker activities during the OpenSOC competition.

Accelerating Log Investigation Workflows

The session highlights practical querying strategies, dashboard visualization techniques, and stream configurations to rapidly isolate indicators of compromise during live incidents.

talks.title: Zeek: OpenSOC CTF Tool Demo
talks.teaser: Shows how to analyze network traffic, extract protocol metadata, and identify malicious connections using Zeek in OpenSOC.
talks.summary:
Network Security Monitoring with Zeek

Zeek converts raw network packets into structured, transaction-level log streams, providing deep protocol visibility without the overhead of full packet capture storage.

Extracting Metadata in OpenSOC Investigations

The demonstration shows how to inspect Zeek connection, DNS, HTTP, and SSL logs to trace malicious traffic flows and spot command-and-control communications during the CTF.

Custom Scripting and Detection Logic

Defenders learn how to leverage Zeek's event-driven scripting language to parse custom protocols, extract file hashes on the wire, and automate alert generation.

talks.title: Velociraptor: OpenSOC CTF Tool Demo
talks.teaser: Demonstrates endpoint hunting, artifact collection, and forensic querying using Velociraptor VQL in OpenSOC.
talks.summary:
Endpoint Visibility with Velociraptor

Velociraptor is an open-source endpoint visibility and digital forensics tool designed for rapid response and fleet-wide interrogation during security incidents.

Forensic Querying with VQL

Using the Velociraptor Query Language (VQL), investigators can formulate expressive queries to inspect running processes, memory allocations, persistence mechanisms, and filesystem artifacts.

Hands-On Triage for OpenSOC Competitors

The demo guides participants through gathering live endpoint evidence, deploying hunting artifacts, and isolating compromised workstations during the OpenSOC defense challenge.

talks.title: Thinkst Canary: OpenSOC CTF Tool Demo
talks.teaser: Shows how deception technology and Thinkst Canary tokens generate high-fidelity alerts during unauthorized network traversal.
talks.summary:
Deception Technology in Modern Networks

Thinkst Canary deployable honeypots and canary tokens act as deceptive tripwires across internal networks, alerting defenders the moment an attacker begins lateral reconnaissance.

Deploying Decoys within OpenSOC

The presentation explores how decoy servers, fake credentials, and breadcrumbs are integrated into the OpenSOC CTF environment to trap adversaries exploring internal network segments.

High-Fidelity Triage and Attribution

Canary alerts provide near-zero false-positive signals, enabling incident response teams to rapidly pinpoint the origin of unauthorized credential usage and host enumeration.

talks.title: Suricata: OpenSOC CTF Tool Demo
talks.teaser: Explains how to write, tune, and inspect Suricata intrusion detection signatures to identify exploit traffic in OpenSOC.
talks.summary:
High-Performance Intrusion Detection

Suricata is a mature, open-source network threat detection engine capable of real-time intrusion detection (IDS), intrusion prevention (IPS), and network security monitoring.

Investigating Alerts in OpenSOC

The demonstration shows how Suricata signatures generate structured EVE JSON output, allowing analysts to triage signature matches and correlate alerts with raw network sessions.

Rule Tuning and Protocol Inspection

Participants learn techniques for refining signature rules, inspecting multi-gigabit traffic streams, and detecting exploit payloads traversing internal and perimeter network interfaces.

talks.title: Moloch: OpenSOC CTF Tool Demo
talks.teaser: Walks through full packet capture analysis, session reconstruction, and PCAP carving using Moloch in OpenSOC.
talks.summary:
Large-Scale Packet Indexing with Moloch

Moloch (now Arkime) is an open-source, large-scale packet capture, indexing, and database system that provides visual browsing and session reconstruction for network traffic.

Session Analysis and Packet Carving

The presenter illustrates how to construct complex SPI search queries, examine reassembled TCP sessions, and carve suspect payloads directly from full packet captures.

Applying Full PCAP to the OpenSOC Challenge

Participants discover how Moloch serves as the definitive source of truth in OpenSOC, validating whether network anomalies triggered by other tools represent true positive intrusions.

talks.title: Detecting the Not-PowerShell Gang
talks.teaser: Uncovers popular Not-PowerShell offensive tools and demonstrates how defenders can spot non-PowerShell tradecraft.
talks.summary:
The Shift Away from PowerShell Tradecraft

Enhanced security visibility in PowerShell version 5—including Script Block Logging, Constrained Language Mode, and AMSI—pushed red teams toward alternative living-off-the-land techniques.

Emergence of Not-PowerShell Tools

Adversaries increasingly adopt compiled C# binaries, direct API invocations, and LOLBAS utilities that bypass standard PowerShell logging and monitoring configurations.

Building Resilient Host Detections

Defenders examine practical detection engineering methods using Sysmon, ETW, and process telemetry to expose unauthorized runtime executions, process injection, and unmanaged code execution.

talks.title: No Question: TeamViewer, Police, and Consequence
talks.teaser: Recounts the investigation and law enforcement aftermath of an internal keylogger breach traced through TeamViewer logs and OSINT.
talks.summary:
Discovering an Internal Network Breach

Following attendance at DEF CON Blue Team Village, an analyst uncovers a massive compromise at a non-profit client where a malicious actor deployed keyloggers across more than a hundred workstations.

Log Parsing and OSINT Attribution

Lacking enterprise SIEM or IDS infrastructure, the responder manually parses server logs, uncovers suspicious TeamViewer connection artifacts, and leverages OSINT to identify the perpetrator's physical residence.

Law Enforcement Engagement and Confession

A criminal dossier handed to local cybercrime investigators leads to a search warrant and a full confession, proving definitively that an insider was behind the widespread deployment.

The Complex Aftermath of Real-World Breaches

Despite conclusive findings, unexpected organizational politics and undisclosed decisions result in no criminal charges being filed, illustrating the challenging real-world dynamics defenders navigate.

talks.title: Osquery: OpenSOC CTF Tool Demo
talks.teaser: Demonstrates using Osquery SQL syntax to query endpoint state and investigate security incidents during the OpenSOC defense CTF.
talks.summary:
Penetration Testing and Attack Techniques

This talk covers penetration testing methodologies and attack techniques. Topics include reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and post-exploitation activities in security assessments.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)
